body.en: The unit circle extends trigonometry to all real numbers. Trigonometric identities are equations true for all values of the variable — they allow simplification, equation solving, and calculus manipulations.

For angle \(\theta\) in standard position, terminal point on unit circle: \((\cos\theta,\sin\theta).\)

\[\sin(\theta+2\pi)=\sin\theta,\quad\cos(\theta+2\pi)=\cos\theta,\quad\tan(\theta+\pi)=\tan\theta.\]

Even/Odd: \(\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta\) (even); \(\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta\) (odd); \(\tan(-\theta)=-\tan\theta\) (odd).

label.en: ▲ Pre-Calculus Traps & Commandments — Unit Circle & Trigonometric Identities

body.en:
• ASTC Quadrant Signs: Remember All Students Take Calculus: Q1 (All positive), Q2 (Sine positive, Cos/Tan negative), Q3 (Tangent positive, Sin/Cos negative), Q4 (Cosine positive, Sin/Tan negative).
  • Pythagorean Identity Sign Determination: When solving \(\cos\theta = \pm\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\theta}\), actively select the sign based on the quadrant of \(\theta\). Never leave \(\pm\) in an evaluated expression.
  • Never Divide by a Variable Trig Function: In equations like \(\sin(2\theta) = \sin\theta\), never divide both sides by \(\sin\theta\). Doing so eliminates roots where \(\sin\theta = 0\)! Instead, expand \(2\sin\theta\cos\theta - \sin\theta = 0\) and factor out \(\sin\theta\).
  • Double-Angle Cosine Selection: \(\cos(2\theta)\) has three interchangeable identities: \(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\). Choose the identity that matches the other trigonometric functions in the equation to form a solvable single-variable quadratic.

question.en: Solve the trigonometric equation \(\cos(2\theta) + 3\sin\theta = 2\) for all solutions \(\theta \in [0, 2\pi)\).

solution.en:
Substitute \(\cos(2\theta) = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\) to express the entire equation in terms of \(\sin\theta\):

\[(1 - 2\sin^2\theta) + 3\sin\theta = 2.\]\[-2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0.\]

Factor the quadratic in \(\sin\theta\):

\[(2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0.\]

Case 1: \(2\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}\). On \([0, 2\pi)\), \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\) or \(\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}\).

Case 2: \(\sin\theta - 1 = 0 \implies \sin\theta = 1\). On \([0, 2\pi)\), \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

Combining all solutions: \(\theta \in \left\{\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{6}\right\}\).

question.en: Verify the trigonometric identity: \[\frac{\sin(2x)}{\sin x} - \frac{\cos(2x)}{\cos x} = \sec x.\]

solution.en:
Expand the double-angle expressions on the left-hand side:

\[\text{LHS} = \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\sin x} - \frac{2\cos^2 x - 1}{\cos x}.\]

Cancel \(\sin x\) in the first term and combine over a common denominator of \(\cos x\):

\[= 2\cos x - \frac{2\cos^2 x - 1}{\cos x} = \frac{2\cos^2 x - (2\cos^2 x - 1)}{\cos x}.\]\[= \frac{2\cos^2 x - 2\cos^2 x + 1}{\cos x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x = \text{RHS}. \quad \checkmark\]
